questions.title: Fixed Brand Motto Printer
questions.description:
Declare a string `motto` initialized to the literal "AtomCode Rocks" and print it as many times as the input integer n specifies, each on its own line.

Input Format:
A single line containing a positive integer n.

Output Format:
The motto printed n times, each on its own line.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100
questions.sampleoutput1:
AtomCode Rocks
AtomCode Rocks
AtomCode Rocks
questions.output1:
AtomCode Rocks
AtomCode Rocks
AtomCode Rocks
AtomCode Rocks
AtomCode Rocks
questions.output3:
AtomCode Rocks
AtomCode Rocks
AtomCode Rocks
AtomCode Rocks

questions.title: Single Word Echo Drill
questions.description:
Read a single word (no spaces) from stdin using scanf and print it back exactly as read on its own line.

Input Format:
A single line containing one word (no spaces).

Output Format:
The same word on its own line.

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 1000

questions.title: Manual String Length Counter
questions.description:
Read a single word and count its length manually by traversing characters until the null terminator. Do NOT use strlen. Print the length as an integer.

Input Format:
A single line containing one word (no spaces).

Output Format:
A single integer — the length of the word.

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 1000

questions.title: Manual String Equality Drill
questions.description:
Read two words and determine whether they are equal by comparing them character-by-character. Do NOT use strcmp. Print "Equal" if they match exactly (same length and same characters), otherwise print "NotEqual".

Input Format:
A single line containing two space-separated words.

Output Format:
The word "Equal" or "NotEqual" on its own line.

Constraints:
1 <= length of each word <= 1000
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of each word <= 1000, no spaces inside words

questions.title: String Length via strlen
questions.description:
Read a single word and print its length using the standard library strlen function from string.h.

Input Format:
A single line containing one word (no spaces).

Output Format:
A single integer — the length of the word.

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 1000

questions.title: Uppercase via toupper Drill
questions.description:
Read a single word of lowercase English letters and convert each character to uppercase using the toupper function from ctype.h. Print the result.

Input Format:
A single line containing one lowercase word.

Output Format:
The uppercase version of the word on its own line.

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 1000, lowercase letters only

questions.title: Coffee Shop Brand Card Printer
questions.description:
A coffee shop prints a branded receipt header. Declare two initialized strings: brand = "Bean & Brew Cafe" and tagline = "Freshly Roasted Daily". Read the number of coffees ordered and print the brand header, the tagline, and "Orders: <n>" on three separate lines.

Input Format:
A single line containing a positive integer n.

Output Format:
Three lines:
Line 1: the brand string
Line 2: the tagline string
Line 3: "Orders: <n>"

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000

Bean & Brew Cafe
Freshly Roasted Daily
Orders: 3

Orders: 1

Bean & Brew Cafe

questions.title: Boarding Pass Passenger Echo
questions.description:
An airport kiosk reads a passenger's first name and a flight code (both single tokens) from stdin and prints a boarding pass header line.

Input Format:
A single line containing two space-separated tokens: the passenger's first name and the flight code.

Output Format:
A single line in the form "Passenger <name> Flight <flight>".

Constraints:
1 <= length of each token <= 50
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of each token <= 50, no spaces inside tokens

questions.title: Username Length Reporter
questions.description:
A registration form reads a username (single word) and reports its length. Traverse the string manually to count characters (do NOT use strlen) and print "Length: <n>".

Input Format:
A single line containing one username word.

Output Format:
A single line: "Length: <n>".

Constraints:
1 <= username length <= 1000

questions.title: Username Lowercase Normalizer
questions.description:
A login form normalizes usernames by converting all letters to lowercase using the tolower function from ctype.h. Read a username (single word, may contain mixed case) and print the normalized version.

Input Format:
A single line containing one username word.

Output Format:
The lowercase version of the username on its own line.

Constraints:
1 <= username length <= 1000

questions.title: Passport Number Builder
questions.description:
A passport office issues passport numbers in the format "PAS-<country>-<serial>" where country is a 3-letter code and serial is a 6-digit number. Declare a fixed prefix "PAS-" as an initialized string and use strcpy and strcat to assemble the final passport number. Do NOT use sprintf or snprintf.

Input Format:
A single line containing two space-separated tokens: the country code and the serial number.

Output Format:
A single line: "PAS-<country>-<serial>".

Constraints:
Country is exactly 3 uppercase letters; serial is exactly 6 digits.
questions.inputconstrains: Country is 3 uppercase letters; serial is 6 digits

questions.title: License Plate Token Reader
questions.description:
A parking lot kiosk reads a vehicle's license plate and a vehicle type from two separate lines using fgets (NOT scanf). Strip the trailing newline from each line manually and print a single summary line: "<type>: <plate>".

Input Format:
Two lines:
Line 1: the license plate (single token, no spaces)
Line 2: the vehicle type (single token, no spaces)

Output Format:
A single line: "<type>: <plate>".

Constraints:
1 <= length of each token <= 50
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of each token <= 50, no spaces inside tokens

questions.title: Tagline Length Cutoff Inspector
questions.description:
A registration form allows a tagline up to 20 characters. Read the tagline (a single line, may contain spaces) using fgets. Traverse it manually (do NOT use strlen or strcspn) to count characters after stripping the trailing newline. If the length is at most 20, print "ACCEPT <length>"; otherwise print "REJECT <length>".

Input Format:
A single line containing the tagline (may contain spaces).

Output Format:
A single line: either "ACCEPT <length>" or "REJECT <length>".

Constraints:
1 <= tagline length <= 1000
questions.input1: This tagline is way too long for the cutoff

questions.title: SKU Equality Checker
questions.description:
An inventory system checks whether two scanned SKU codes match exactly. Read two SKUs (single tokens) and compare them character-by-character without using strcmp or any of its variants. Print "MATCH" if they are identical (same length and same characters), otherwise "NOMATCH".

Input Format:
A single line containing two space-separated SKUs.

Output Format:
A single line: "MATCH" or "NOMATCH".

Constraints:
1 <= length of each SKU <= 50
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of each SKU <= 50, no spaces inside SKUs

questions.title: Product Code Assembler with strcat
questions.description:
A warehouse assembles a product code from three tokens: category, brand, and model. Declare the fixed prefix "PRODUCT-" as an initialized string. Use strcpy and strcat (do NOT use sprintf or snprintf) to assemble the final code in the form "PRODUCT-<category>-<brand>-<model>".

Input Format:
A single line containing three space-separated tokens: category, brand, model.

Output Format:
A single line: "PRODUCT-<category>-<brand>-<model>".

Constraints:
1 <= length of each token <= 30
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of each token <= 30, no spaces inside tokens

questions.title: Swapcase Text Transformer
questions.description:
A text formatter applies swapcase to a line of text — every uppercase letter becomes lowercase and every lowercase letter becomes uppercase, using toupper and tolower from ctype.h. Read a single line of text (may contain spaces) and print the swapcased version. Do NOT use 'A' or 'a' character literals for case detection — use isupper / islower.

Input Format:
A single line of text.

Output Format:
The swapcased line on its own line.

Constraints:
1 <= text length <= 1000

questions.title: Inventory SKU Family Generator
questions.description:
A warehouse generates a family of 3 related SKUs from a 2-character category code and a serial number. Each SKU has the form "SKU-<category>-<serial>-<tier>" where tier is one of "BASIC", "STD", or "PRO". Declare the prefix "SKU-" as an initialized string and declare the three tier strings via a char-pointer array initialized with string literals. Use strcpy and strcat (do NOT use sprintf or snprintf) to assemble each SKU. Print each SKU on its own line, in the order BASIC, STD, PRO.

Input Format:
A single line containing two space-separated tokens: the 2-character category code and the serial number.

Output Format:
Three lines, one per SKU tier, in the order BASIC, STD, PRO.

Constraints:
Category is exactly 2 characters; 1 <= serial length <= 10
questions.inputconstrains: Category is exactly 2 characters; 1 <= serial length <= 10

questions.title: PAN Number Format Validator
questions.description:
An Indian PAN (Permanent Account Number) is a 10-character code with a strict format: positions 1-5 are uppercase letters (A-Z), positions 6-9 are digits (0-9), and position 10 is an uppercase letter. Read a PAN string (single token) and validate this format by manual traversal. Do NOT use strlen or any of the is* functions (isalpha, isdigit, isalnum) — check character ranges with 'A'-'Z' and '0'-'9' comparisons and the logical AND operator. Print "VALID" or "INVALID".

Input Format:
A single line containing one PAN string.

Output Format:
A single line: "VALID" or "INVALID".

Constraints:
1 <= PAN length <= 30

questions.title: Lexicographic SKU Sorter
questions.description:
An inventory sorter reads 3 SKUs and outputs them in ascending lexicographic (dictionary) order. Implement a manual character-by-character comparison helper (do NOT use strcmp, strncmp, strcasecmp, memcmp, or qsort) and use it to sort the three SKUs via pointer-swap. Print the sorted SKUs one per line.

Input Format:
A single line containing three space-separated SKUs.

Output Format:
Three lines, the SKUs sorted in ascending lexicographic order.

Constraints:
1 <= length of each SKU <= 50
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of each SKU <= 50, no spaces inside SKUs

questions.title: Camel to Snake Identifier Formatter
questions.description:
A code formatter converts a camelCase identifier (single word) to snake_case. For each uppercase letter encountered, output an underscore followed by the lowercase version (using tolower from ctype.h). Lowercase letters and other characters pass through unchanged. Use isupper from ctype.h to detect uppercase letters — do NOT use 'A' or 'a' character literals for case detection.

Input Format:
A single line containing one camelCase identifier.

Output Format:
The snake_case version of the identifier on its own line.

Constraints:
1 <= identifier length <= 100
